quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color are the pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines are painted in the center of the road. They separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians crossing on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side traffic is moving on.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road unless a sign says otherwise?

options.text: 20 mph.
40 mph.
55 mph.
70 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road is 55 miles per hour. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You must come to a full stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed first when you cannot see well or when road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can go when it is safe.

questions.question: How far from a crosswalk or intersection must you stay when parking?

options.text: 10 feet
25 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 10 feet of a crosswalk or intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be present in the area.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center of your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, honk your horn first to get the driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because if the other driver corrects at the last moment, you will still crash. If a crash cannot be stopped, brake hard and steady. Slowing down even a little reduces the impact.

questions.question: What is most important to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to control in a curve due to inertia. You must slow down before entering the curve to stay in control.

questions.question: What should you do first when parallel parking between two cars?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After you find a space, check traffic, and signal, stop parallel to the car in front of your parking space before turning your wheels.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: Signs placed wherever there is danger.
Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
Diamond-shaped signs that are yellow or green.
Signs that warn you about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs that tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. These signs show speed limits, no passing rules, no turning rules, and other driving laws.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. The road will split into two one-way lanes separated by a median. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What is a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
It does not require you to slow down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles marking lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones are marked with orange signs with black lettering. Slow down and pay attention when you see or drive through a work zone.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?

options.text: A road hazard sign.
An interstate route sign.
A school crossing sign.
A speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and usually yellow. In work areas, they may be orange. These signs warn you about hazards or places where special driving rules apply.

questions.question: When you approach a roundabout, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Stop completely.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed for low-speed driving.

questions.question: You turn left onto a one-way street. Which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: What is true about crosswalks?

options.text: They always have lines painted on the road.
They always have vertical lines painted on the road.
They never have any markings.
They may have painted lines or no markings at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may have painted lines or no markings at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist with or without painted lines. You must stop behind a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross.

questions.question: Which does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: How well you can steer.
How far you travel while braking.
How far you travel while reacting.
How long it takes you to notice a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: How well you can steer.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how long it takes you to notice a problem, how long it takes you to react, and how far you travel while braking. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What should drivers do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Yield to cars entering the roundabout.
Drive clockwise around the center.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that flows counterclockwise around a center island. It usually has no traffic signal. When you enter, you must yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.
